A severe winter storm/cold snap affected Texas during February 12–17.
nodes.quote: Texas had one of, if not the, coldest and most impactful winter storms observed in state history during the week of February 12–17.

nodes.label: Record winter demand and generation unit outages cascaded into grid instability and power losses across ERCOT.
nodes.quote: A combination of record winter demand and generation unit outages cascaded into instability and power losses across the ERCOT power grid

nodes.label: At the peak, 4.5 million Texans were without electricity.
nodes.quote: resulting in 4.5 million Texans without electricity at the peak.

nodes.label: Natural gas production fell significantly during the event, and power outages made the decline worse.
nodes.quote: Although natural gas production fell significantly during this event, the timeline indicates that power outages made this decline worse.

nodes.label: All power generation resources showed lower output during the worst of the cold snap while demand peaked.
nodes.quote: During the worst of the cold snap, all power generation resources showed a decline in output while demand peaked to unprecedented levels.

nodes.label: ERCOT meteorologists reportedly warned market participants and the public of the year's coldest weather.
nodes.quote: ERCOT meteorologists reportedly warns Market Participants and the public of the coldest weather of the year.

nodes.label: ERCOT issued an Operating Conditions Notice for an approaching extreme cold weather system.
nodes.quote: February 8: ERCOT issues an Operating Conditions Notice (OCN) for an extreme cold weather system approaching Thursday, February 11 through Monday, February 15 with temperatures anticipated to remain 32° F or below.

nodes.quote: February 10: ERCOT issues an Advisory for the predicted extreme weather for the ERCOT Region.

nodes.quote: February 12: Governor Greg Abbott declares a state of emergency in all Texas counties ahead of the expected severe winter weather.

nodes.quote: Natural gas supply declined ~0.2 Bcf/d and ~0.7 Bcf/d on February 12 and 13, respectively, leading up to February 14.

nodes.label: Power generation failures occurred across the board.
nodes.quote: The declines on February 13, although material, were not large enough to cause the power generation failures seen across the board.
